parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Start from what magnetic flux density does - it tells you how much force a current in a field feels. What three things must the force depend on?
Hint 2: A unit definition needs a number 1 for each quantity and a special condition on direction. When is the force $F = BIL$ at its maximum?
parts.proper_answer: 1 T is the magnetic flux density that exerts a force of 1 N per metre on a conductor carrying a current of 1 A placed perpendicular to the field.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link B to force on a wire**
Think of $B$ as force per unit current per unit length. For a straight wire the magnetic force is $$F = BIL\sin\theta$$ where $\theta$ is the angle between current and field.

Step 2: **Set everything to 1 and fix the angle**
One tesla means when $I = 1\text{ A}$, $L = 1\text{ m}$ and $\sin\theta = 1$, the force is $1\text{ N}$. $\sin\theta = 1$ means $\theta = 90^{\circ}$, so the wire is perpendicular to the field. That gives $1\text{ T} = 1\text{ N A}^{-1}\text{ m}^{-1}$ for the perpendicular case.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A stiff metal wire is used to form a rectangular frame measuring $8.0\text{ cm} \times 6.0\text{ cm}$. The frame is open at the top, and is suspended from a sensitive newton meter, as shown in Fig. 8.1.

{{figure:figure_8_1}}

Fig. 8.1

The open ends of the frame are connected to a power supply so that there is a current of $5.0\text{ A}$ in the frame in the direction indicated in Fig. 8.1.

The frame is slowly lowered into a uniform magnetic field of flux density $B$ so that all of side $PQ$ is in the field. The magnetic field lines are horizontal and at an angle of $50^{\circ}$ to $PQ$, as shown in Fig. 8.2.

{{figure:figure_8_2}}

Fig. 8.2

When side $PQ$ of the frame first enters the magnetic field, the reading on the newton meter changes by $1.0\text{ mN}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Determine the magnetic flux density $B$, in $\text{mT}$.
hints: Hint 1: Only side PQ is in the field at first. Identify $F$, $I$ and $L$ for that side - what is the length PQ in metres and what is the extra force in newtons?
Hint 2: The field is not at $90^{\circ}$ to the current. Look at Fig. 8.2 for the angle between $I$ along PQ and $B$, then rearrange $F = BIL\sin\theta$ for $B$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Pick out the active length**
Only PQ is in the uniform field, so $L = 6.0\text{ cm} = 0.060\text{ m}$. The magnetic force on it is what changes the newton meter reading, so $$F = 1.0\text{ mN} = 1.0\times 10^{-3}\text{ N}$$ Current $I = 5.0\text{ A}$.

Step 2: **Use F = BIL sin theta**
From the top view, the angle between current along PQ and $B$ is $\theta = 50^{\circ}$. The component of $B$ perpendicular to the current causes the force: $$F = BIL\sin\theta$$ Rearrange before numbers: $$B = \frac{F}{IL\sin\theta}$$

Step 3: **Calculate**
$$B = \frac{1.0\times 10^{-3}}{5.0 \times 0.060 \times \sin 50^{\circ}} \approx 4.35\times 10^{-3}\text{ T}$$ So $B \approx 4.4\text{ mT}$ to 2 s.f.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State, with a reason, whether the change in the reading on the newton meter is an increase or a decrease.
hints: Hint 1: Use Fleming's left-hand rule on side PQ with current from P to Q and $B$ as in Fig. 8.2. Remember $B$ is horizontal and current is horizontal, so which way - up or down - must the force point?
parts.proper_answer: Decrease. By Fleming's left-hand rule the magnetic force on PQ is vertically upwards, so it supports part of the weight and reduces the tension measured by the newton meter.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find force direction**
Current flows from P to Q, to the right. $B$ is horizontal at $50^{\circ}$ to PQ. Point your First finger along $B$, Second finger along current. Your Thumb then points vertically upwards, out of the horizontal plane. So the magnetic force on PQ is up.

Step 2: **Link to meter reading**
The newton meter reads the pull needed to support the frame. An extra upward magnetic force helps support it, so less tension is needed and the reading decreases by $1.0\text{ mN}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The frame is lowered further so that the vertical sides start to enter the magnetic field.

Suggest what effect this will have on the frame.

markscheme_points.text: frame will rotate (so that PQ beco

hints: Hint 1: Think about the two vertical sides together - the current runs down on the left and up on the right while both sit in the same horizontal $B$ field. What does that tell you about the pair of forces?
parts.proper_answer: The frame will rotate (about a vertical axis). The opposite currents in the two vertical sides give opposite lateral magnetic forces, forming a couple that twists the frame.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Spot the couple**
Once the vertical sides enter the field, you have current down on one side and up on the other in the same $B$ field. By Fleming's left-hand rule the magnetic forces on them are sideways and in opposite directions.

Step 2: **Result is rotation not just a pull**
Two equal, opposite, separated forces make a couple. So instead of just changing the vertical pull, the frame will twist or rotate about a vertical axis, tending to turn PQ relative to the field direction.
